brief: Verdict ahead of the print: consensus expects 3Q26 revenue of about $20.7bn, up about 17% on 3Q25's $17,638mn, and adjusted EPS of about $7.03, up 42% on $4.95. The stock will trade on backlog (the $72.1bn record at 30 June), Power Generation growth, and whether margins hold up now that the $392mn IEEPA tariff recovery that lifted 2Q26 is gone. Shares closed at $687.00 on 23 October, down 2.42% on the day and 36% below the $1,073.46 52-week high.

Where expectations sit. Yahoo Finance shows 3Q26 EPS of $7.03 from 22 analysts (range $6.23 to $8.48) and revenue of $20.69bn from 12 (range $19.96bn to $23.07bn). MarketBeat has $7.04 and $20.76bn, and Fiscal.ai (via Stocktwits, 5 October) had about $6.92 and $20.40bn. The quarterly EPS consensus has risen from $6.48 90 days ago. FY26 consensus is $27.33 EPS and $79.6bn revenue (up 17.8%, inside the mid-to-high-teens guide), and FY27 is $32.59 and $88.67bn. No consensus was found for Power & Energy segment sales or margin, Power Generation sales, orders or backlog.

What the company guided for 3Q26 (2Q26 call, 4 August): strong sales growth year on year in all three primary segments, a higher adjusted operating margin than 3Q25's 17.5%, and tariff costs of about $600mn, similar to 3Q25. Power & Energy margin should rise year on year on volume and price, partly offset by depreciation and costs from the capacity expansion. For FY26: sales up mid-to-high teens; adjusted operating margin near the bottom of the target range excluding IEEPA recoveries (about 18.8% to 22.8% at $79.6bn of sales, interpolated from the 18% to 22% band at $72bn and 21% to 25% at $100bn); MP&E free cash flow in the top half of the $6bn to $15bn range; tariffs of about $2.2bn; capex of about $3.5bn.

Three debates. First, data center durability: Baird downgraded on 29 July, citing local moratoria and pushback, and Truist cut its target on 5 October over the durability of power, data center and AI spending. Management said in August that no customer had backed off, and Citi calls the worries overblown. Second, capacity versus demand: gas prime gensets are with lead times into late 2028 and turbines run longer, a restarted 10 MW engine line adds about 1.5 GW from 4Q26, and large-engine capacity rises to nearly 3x 2024 by 2030. Bears ask whether that capacity arrives as orders peak. Third, margin quality: 2Q26's 21.9% adjusted margin included the $392mn tariff recovery, and the guide is near the bottom of the band without it.

What would move the stock. Positive: backlog above $72.1bn with Power & Energy the main contributor, Power Generation growth at or above 2Q's 29%, a Power & Energy margin near 2Q's 24.6%, and the FY26 guide raised. Negative: a flat or lower backlog, any customer deferral or cancellation of data center orders, slippage in the 10 MW restart, or margin pressure from capacity costs and tariffs. Options imply a move of about 7.8% on the print (earnings-watcher, 23 October), about $54 on a $687 share price.

Kona read-through. Caterpillar's gas prime genset slots run into late 2028 and turbines run longer, and distant orders carry price escalators. At tens of MW, Kona competes for the same slots as gigawatt data center buyers. It should expect long reservations, indexed prices and vendor financing as the main commercial terms.
changes: The stock fell from $863.44 on 6 October to $687.00 on 23 October (StockAnalysis). Truist cut its target from $1,225 to $1,100 on 5 October (shares fell 5.7% on 7 October, to $813.83), and Citi cut from $1,100 to $950 on 12 October. On 22 October shares fell 4.89% to $704.05 in a sector-wide power-equipment selloff with no company news (TIKR).

Leadership: Derrick York, president of Solar Turbines, becomes group president of Resource Industries on 1 November 2026, replacing the retiring Denise Johnson (8-K, 15 October 2026). The filing names no successor at Solar Turbines.

Caterpillar and Cat Financial renewed $11.5bn of undrawn revolving credit lines on 27 August 2026: $3.5bn 364-day, $3.0bn three-year (due 2029) and $5.0bn five-year (due 2031) (8-K, 1 September 2026).

CEO Joe Creed sold 32,401 shares on 28 August at an average of $808.98, about $26.2mn (MarketBeat). At a conference on 10 September he described supply as 'hand to mouth' with little slack (TIKR, single source).

Deliveries on the AIP Monarch campus (2 GW of G3516 gas gensets, West Virginia) are scheduled from September 2026 to August 2027, with Caterpillar Financial providing vendor equipment financing (Data Center Dynamics, January 2026).

No post-results material was read. Independent check: a separate fact-check agent, given only the draft and sources, re-confirmed about 15 core figures (consensus, 2Q26 actuals, backlog, debt and credit lines, outlook, 23 October price, AIP Monarch order, 2055 bond estimate) and recomputed derived figures; the 7 October move was corrected to 5.7% and 'sold out' changed to lead-time language. consensus_thesis: Investors own Caterpillar as the diversified way into AI data center power: gas gensets and Solar turbines with lead times into late 2028 and beyond, capacity rising to nearly 3x 2024 for large engines and 2.5x for turbines, and a 2030 Power Generation target of more than 3x 2024 sales. At $687.00 (about $316bn market cap, about 25.1x Yahoo's FY26 EPS of $27.33 and 21.1x FY27's $32.59), the valuation pays for revenue rising from $67.6bn in 2025 to about $79.6bn in FY26 and $88.7bn in FY27. Positioning has turned contested: the stock is 36% off its 30 June peak, Baird is at Neutral, Michael Burry disclosed a short, Truist and Citi have cut targets, and the Street is split 15 Buy to 12 Hold (MarketBeat). Credit is not the debate: Caterpillar's 5.5% 2055 notes are estimated (not traded) at about 95.1, a yield of about 5.86% and a spread of about 52bp on 23 October (TheRightTrader model).
headline: 3Q26 will be judged less on a roughly $20.7bn revenue quarter (up about 17%) than on whether the $72.1bn backlog keeps growing and Power Generation keeps compounding without IEEPA tariff help. The stock closed at $687.00 on 23 October, 36% below its $1,073.46 high, after target cuts and a sector-wide selloff over data center durability.
kona: Caterpillar's gas prime gensets have lead times into late 2028, turbines longer, and distant orders carry price escalators tied to economic indicators. Caterpillar does not publish $/kW, and no sourced price was found. At tens of MW, Kona will be competing with gigawatt data center buyers for slots, so a new-build Caterpillar island likely means a reservation now for 2028 delivery, at a price that is indexed rather than fixed. The 1.5 GW restart of the 10 MW engine from 4Q26, dealer channels and rental fleets are the faster routes to check. Caterpillar Financial's vendor financing on the 2 GW AIP order is a precedent Kona can ask for: OEM credit in place of, or alongside, project debt.

name: Caterpillar

questions.question: In August you said 59% of the $72.1bn backlog ships within 12 months and that gas prime gensets are with lead times into late 2028, but you do not disclose the backlog by segment or the data center share. How much of the 30 September backlog is Power & Energy, and how much of that is for data centers? What share of data center orders carry cancellation fees or non-refundable deposits? Has any data center customer deferred or cancelled an order since July, yes or no, and for how many MW?
questions.why: The multiple rests on Power Generation reaching more than 3x 2024 sales by 2030. Without a segment backlog and its terms, investors cannot tell firm demand from options, and that gap is the core of the Baird and Burry bear case.

questions.question: Power & Energy margin was 24.6% in 2Q26, and you guided 3Q margin higher year on year despite capacity-related depreciation, while large-engine capacity goes to nearly 3x 2024 and turbines to 2.5x. What price realization did Power & Energy earn in 3Q, in dollars? What is the escalator formula on 2028 to 2030 deliveries? If data center orders slowed in 2027, what segment margin would the added capacity support at 2025 volumes?
questions.why: This tests whether margin gains are structural (pricing power in a sold-out market) or cyclical (volume over a fixed cost base that is now expanding). Capacity added at the peak is how earnings power reverses in this industry.

questions.question: Caterpillar Financial is providing vendor financing on the 2 GW AIP order of G3516 gensets, with deliveries from September 2026 to August 2027. How much Cat Financial exposure to data center developers and power projects is on the book at 30 September, or committed? What share is with non-investment-grade or project-level borrowers? What is the largest single exposure? Will you cap this lending as a share of Cat Financial's roughly $35bn of receivables?
questions.why: Cat Financial runs at about 9.8x debt to equity under a 10.0x covenant. If it becomes the lender of last resort for data center developers, the risk of a slowdown moves from lost orders into credit losses on a highly leveraged finance arm.

questions.question: You plan MP&E free cash flow in the top half of $6bn to $15bn and to return substantially all of it, after $6.5bn of buybacks in H1, while capex rises to about $3.5bn and Cat Financial debt is about $34.5bn. What minimum enterprise cash and what ratings do you run to? If data center orders fell 30% in 2027, would buybacks or capacity capex give way first? Give a number for the 2027 capex plan.
questions.why: Bondholders price Caterpillar tightly (an estimated spread of about 52bp on the 2055 notes). The risk to them is cash returned at the peak while capex commitments and vendor financing grow at the same time.

questions.question: Excluding the $392mn IEEPA recovery, 2Q26 adjusted margin would have been well below the reported 21.9%. You guide FY26 near the bottom of the band, about 18.8% at consensus sales, while sales are tracking toward the top of the mid-to-high-teens growth range. Why is the margin not higher at those volumes? What would you need to reach the midpoint in 2027: price, tariff relief or volume? Will tariff costs in 2027 be above or below $2.2bn?
questions.why: Consensus EPS growth of 42% in 3Q needs incremental margins to hold without one-off recoveries. A guide near the bottom of the band despite top-of-range sales challenges the operating-leverage pillar.

questions.question: Derrick York leaves Solar Turbines on 1 November, just as turbine capacity is going to 2.5x 2024 and turbine lead times are longer than for gas gensets. Who runs Solar Turbines from 1 November? Is the turbine expansion on schedule, in MW per year? For a new customer ordering a Titan 130 or Titan 350 package today, what is the earliest delivery quarter?
questions.why: Turbines are the longest-lead product in the data center power stack and the biggest capacity bet. A leadership change during the ramp is an execution risk the market has not priced.

risks: Data center demand durability: local moratoria and pushback (Baird), AI-capex worries (Truist), and no disclosure of the data center share of backlog.
Capacity arriving at the peak: large engines going to nearly 3x 2024 and turbines to 2.5x, with capacity-related depreciation already weighing on the 3Q Power & Energy margin.
Margin quality: about $2.2bn of 2026 tariffs, no further IEEPA recoveries assumed, and a guide near the bottom of the band.
Cat Financial exposure to data center developers through vendor financing (AIP, 2 GW), on a finance arm with debt about 9.8x equity against a 10.0x covenant.

Execution and leadership: the 10 MW restart (first shipments in 4Q26), a 'hand to mouth' supply chain (single source), the Solar Turbines succession, and a Construction dealer inventory cut of more than $1bn in 4Q26.

sections.body: Caterpillar sells machines, engines, gensets and turbines through 150 independent dealers, and it earns a services stream of $24bn in 2025 against a $30bn target for 2030. From 2026 it reports Construction Industries, Resource Industries (now including Rail) and Power & Energy, plus Financial Products. Power & Energy had 2025 sales of $28.6bn, with external sales split 43% Power Generation, 32% Oil & Gas and 25% Industrial. It sells reciprocating gensets (G3516, G3520K, up to 10 MW) and Solar Turbines (1 to 39 MW; Titan 350 up to 38 MW). In data centers, diesel gensets still serve backup, while gas gensets and turbines serve prime power. Power revenue is units times price per kW plus services, and distant orders carry price escalators. Caterpillar returns substantially all MP&E free cash flow ($9.5bn in 2025). Cat Financial ($34.5bn of debt) funds customers, including vendor financing on data center power orders.

sections.body: Report timing: the company says results come at 5:30 am CDT on 29 October, with the call at 7:30 am CDT. A 5 October Stocktwits article (via Fiscal.ai) gave 4 November, and XTB said 29 October after the close; both are wrong. 3Q26 EPS runs from about $6.92 (Fiscal.ai, 5 October) to $7.03 (Yahoo) and $7.04 (MarketBeat), and revenue from $20.40bn to $20.76bn. FY26 EPS is $27.33 on Yahoo and S&P Global against $27.74 at MarketBeat, and FY27 is $32.59 against $33.46. Average targets range from $933.64 (S&P Global, 29 analysts, rated Buy) to $967.83 (MarketBeat, Moderate Buy) and about $946 (TIKR). Citi's target is $950 after a 12 October cut from $1,100; an earlier Stocktwits piece still shows $1,100. Power Generation growth in 2Q26 is 29% on segment sales but 72% on sales to users (dealer retail), and press uses the two interchangeably. Some articles call the AIP order 'turbines', but the source says G3516 gensets. The 23 October close is $687.00 on Yahoo and StockAnalysis, against $686.79 (AOL) and $685.37 (Fool snapshot). Lead times are 'late 2028' for gas prime (transcript) but 'into 2029' in Trefis's paraphrase.

sections.body: At 30 June 2026: enterprise cash of $6,713mn. MP&E long-term debt was $10,655mn plus a $35mn current portion. Financial Products debt was $34,456mn ($5,046mn short-term, $8,026mn current portion of long-term debt, $21,384mn long-term). Undrawn credit lines total $11.5bn ($3.5bn 364-day to August 2027, $3.0bn to August 2029, $5.0bn to August 2031), with covenants of Caterpillar net worth of at least $9bn and Cat Financial interest coverage above 1.15x and leverage no higher than 10.0x. Cat Financial's derived debt to equity is about 9.8x. Cat Financial: past dues 1.31% (lowest since 1998, per the CFO), allowance $294mn, H1 write-offs $88mn, and receivables of about $35.1bn gross. It provides vendor financing on the 2 GW AIP genset order. Capital return: H1 buybacks of $6,522mn cash paid (including $1.6bn outstanding under accelerated repurchases), a $1.63 quarterly dividend (raised 8%) and 459.7mn shares at 30 June. MP&E capex is about $3.5bn in 2026. The 5.5% 2055 notes are estimated at about 95.1 (yield about 5.86%, spread about 52bp) on 23 October by TheRightTrader; this is a model estimate, not a trade price. No CDS quote or dated rating action was found.
